toolsAdded.name: ask_user
toolsAdded.description: Ask the user one question and wait for their answer. Give options when the answer is one of a few choices; leave them out for the user to answer in their own words.

question.description: The question, as the user should read it.

options.description: The answers the user can choose from, if any.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__glass__list_pull_requests
toolsAdded.description: Lists the user's PR lists in Glass: PRs that need their review, their own PRs, and PRs they are reviewing, grouped by followed repository.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__glass__list_queue
toolsAdded.description: Lists the PRs in the user's Queue: the PRs they lined up to review next, in order, each with the Revision Glass last saw.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__glass__list_to_dos
toolsAdded.description: Lists the user's To-dos in Glass, done or not, with their notes.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__glass__list_recent_activity
toolsAdded.description: Lists the user's most recent Activity in Glass, newest first: PRs they opened, reviewed, and commented on, and other work they did.

limit.description: How many Activities to list, at most 100.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__glass__list_agents
toolsAdded.description: Lists the user's Agents: the named coding conversations working in a repository, with each one's repository, base branch, program, and whether it waits for the user's answer.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__glass__list_needs_you
toolsAdded.description: Lists what waits on the user in Glass now: Agents with a Permission request or Question waiting, questions from an agent outside Glass, queued PRs whose Agent review is finished, and the user's own PRs with changes requested, failing checks, review threads awaiting their reply, or ready to merge. Agents and outside questions come first, then the longest waiting.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__glass__list_started_work
toolsAdded.description: Lists the Agents and Agent reviews this conversation started, or Agents it messaged, oldest first: each with its state now and the user's message that asked for it. Answer how the work you started is going from this, not from the chat. Agents and reviews the user started themselves, and deleted Agents, aren't listed.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__glass__read_agent_transcript
toolsAdded.description: Reads an Agent's most recent Turns: each message the user sent, what the Agent wrote and which tools it used, and how the Turn ended. Includes Queued messages not yet delivered.

turns.description: How many of the latest Turns to read, at most 20.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__glass__read_pull_request
toolsAdded.description: Reads a PR's title, description, changed files with their diffs, and published Discussions at one Revision. Pass the Revision the user means, such as the one in a message's glass_context; leave it out to read the PR as it is now.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__glass__read_agent_review
toolsAdded.description: Reads a PR's Agent review: the latest one written, with the Revision it reviewed, and whether one is being written now or failed.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__glass__start_agent_review
toolsAdded.description: Starts an Agent review of a PR at a Revision, as the user would from the PR. It appears beside the PR's diff once written. This returns once the review started, not when it is written, which takes minutes: read_agent_review shows its progress and result, or why it failed, such as the PR having changed since that Revision. Starting one replaces any review being written for the PR, so read_agent_review first and ask the user before replacing one.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__glass__list_agent_places
toolsAdded.description: Lists where the user can start an Agent. An Agent on this device works in a copy of a Local checkout, so its repository must be one of localCheckouts. An Agent in a Sandbox works in any followed repository, in a Sandbox from one of sandboxProviders. Each place runs only the Agent programs listed with it.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__glass__list_agent_options
toolsAdded.description: Lists the base branches and models an Agent can start with, for a repository, place, and Agent program from list_agent_places.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__glass__create_agent
toolsAdded.description: Creates an Agent: a named coding conversation working on a branch of its own, made from a base branch of a repository. It starts its first Turn with the message, and appears in the user's Agents. This returns once Glass created the Agent, not when it finishes its Turn: read_agent_transcript shows its progress. Choose the place, program, base branch, and model from list_agent_places and list_agent_options, never from guesses. If this call fails without saying why, or is cut off, call list_agents before trying again rather than creating a second Agent.

baseBranch.description: The branch the Agent's branch starts from.

place.description: Where the Agent works: on this device, or in a Sandbox from a provider.

engine.description: The Agent program that runs the Agent.

model.description: A model id from list_agent_options, or null for the program's default.

effort.description: One of the model's Efforts, or null for its default.

message.description: The Agent's first message: its task.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__glass__send_agent_message
toolsAdded.description: Sends a message to one of the user's Agents, as the user would from the Agent. An idle Agent starts a Turn with it; a busy Agent keeps it as a Queued message and starts on it after its running Turn. This returns once Glass accepted the message, not when the Agent answers: read_agent_transcript shows its progress. If this call fails without saying why, or is cut off, read the Agent's transcript before sending again rather than sending it twice.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__glass__ask_user
toolsAdded.description: For an agent outside Glass: asks the user a question and waits for their answer in the Glass Inbox, in Stopped on you, under the name the user approved. An Agent Glass launched asks with its own Question tool instead. Waits 10 minutes unless timeoutSeconds is set. timeoutSeconds is a whole number of seconds from 1 to 600. Glass sends a progress notification immediately and every 15 seconds while it waits, so a client that resets its timeout when progress arrives is not cut off before Glass's own limit. Pass a progress token on the call. The result is Answered with the user's answer (by is choice or text), TimedOut when they do not answer in time, or Cancelled when Glass shuts down. A timed out or cancelled question leaves the Inbox. choices are optional. The user can pick one or type their own answer. Each MCP session may have one question waiting.

question.description: The question to show in the Inbox.

anyOf.description: Choices the user can pick. They can still type their own answer. Omit this to ask for text only.
Seconds to wait. Defaults to 600, the most allowed.

toolsAdded.name: mcp__glass__wait_for_release
toolsAdded.description: Waits until Glass releases it. Call it only when the user asks you to.
